person.current_location: Her own home in Burlington, Vermont. Lives alone; Carol visits several times a week.
person.hometown: Burlington, Vermont. Has lived here her entire life.
person.personality: Precise, dry-witted, deeply read. Was Head Librarian of Burlington Public Library for 30 years. Keeps a herb garden with handwritten marker stakes — the mint one reads 'do not trust'. Has a particular love for Mary Oliver. Stubborn about her routines. Slow to open up, but generous once she does.

people_in_their_life.name: George
people_in_their_life.what_makes_them_special: 58-year marriage. Brought her tea every morning without being asked. Pulled the car over for every maple on the foliage drives. Ellie still speaks of him in the present tense.
people_in_their_life.favorite_shared_memory: The annual foliage drive up the Stowe road. In October 2012 he pulled over eleven times. She wrote on the back of the photo: 'G pulled over 11 times. Worth it.'

people_in_their_life.name: Carol
people_in_their_life.what_makes_them_special: Her eldest. Lives nearby. Visits often. Set up Kith. Tends to hover when Ellie is baking — Ellie finds this touching and faintly absurd.
people_in_their_life.favorite_shared_memory: The lemon drizzle day. Carol measured everything wrong and Ellie said nothing — just poured the drizzle over the warm cake. Ruth's recipe; Ellie's annotation: 'Trust the drizzle. — E.M.'

people_in_their_life.name: Daniel
people_in_their_life.what_makes_them_special: Her youngest. Lives in Portland, Oregon. A landscape architect. Easy to be around.
people_in_their_life.favorite_shared_memory: Summer 2024 — all four grandchildren together at his place in Portland.

people_in_their_life.name: Lily
people_in_their_life.what_makes_them_special: Was photographed in summer 2024 holding a Mary Oliver paperback, before Ellie knew she was reading Oliver. This quietly delights Ellie. They read together on Sunday afternoons now.
people_in_their_life.favorite_shared_memory: Lily appearing in the 2024 Portland photo with a Mary Oliver book. Ellie found out later and could not stop smiling.

people_in_their_life.name: Oliver
people_in_their_life.what_makes_them_special: Eldest grandchild. Easy, gentle. Always has his arm around Lily in photos.
people_in_their_life.favorite_shared_memory: Portland, July 2024 — the four grandchildren on Daniel's deck.

people_in_their_life.name: Ruth
people_in_their_life.what_makes_them_special: They have been friends since childhood. Ruth wrote the original lemon drizzle recipe in pencil. They still speak regularly.
people_in_their_life.favorite_shared_memory: The recipe card — Ruth's pencil handwriting, Ellie's ink annotation at the bottom.

daily_life.typical_day: Wakes early. Tea first — always from the blue ceramic mug with the chipped rim, no other. Reads before anything else. The herb garden in the morning if the weather allows. Afternoons slower, sometimes a nap. Reads again in the evening. Mary Oliver on Sunday afternoons.
favorite_foods: Whatever comes from the herb garden
hobbies: Reading — Mary Oliver especially, but widely
The herb garden — rosemary planted 1998, mint, creeping thyme

stories_they_love.title: The foliage drives
stories_they_love.story: Every October, George and Ellie drove the Stowe road to see the maples. George pulled over for every vivid tree. In 2012 he pulled over eleven times. They stopped every year at Bishop's Orchard for apples and cider. She wrote on the back of the 2012 photo: 'G pulled over 11 times. Worth it.'

stories_they_love.title: Trust the drizzle
stories_they_love.story: Ruth's lemon drizzle recipe, written in pencil. Ellie added her own line at the bottom in ink: 'Trust the drizzle. — E.M.' Carol once measured everything wrong when they baked together. Ellie said nothing — just poured the drizzle over the warm cake. Carol still talks about it.

stories_they_love.title: The mint marker
stories_they_love.story: The herb garden has handwritten plant stake markers. The one for mint reads: 'MINT — do not trust.' In Ellie's own handwriting. She wrote it herself and put it in the ground.

stories_they_love.title: Lily and Mary Oliver
stories_they_love.story: A photo from summer 2024 shows Lily, eleven years old, holding a Mary Oliver paperback — before Ellie knew she was reading Oliver. The Sunday afternoon reading sessions came after. When Ellie found out about the photo, she was quietly delighted.

stories_they_love.title: The library nameplate
stories_they_love.story: For thirty years the reference desk placard read 'REFERENCE — Eleanor G. Marsh'. She kept a Mary Oliver quotation card pinned above the desk: the final lines of The Summer Day. A regular patron named Marcus had a Saturday SET ASIDE basket. She remembers him.

things_that_comfort_them: The blue ceramic mug with the chipped rim — her mug, no other
The herb garden — especially the rosemary, which has been there since 1998
Mary Oliver, especially The Summer Day
References to the library — she is proud of that work
topics_to_avoid: George's illness or final weeks — she speaks of him in the present tense and this is kind
Whether she can still live alone — her greatest fear
Any suggestion her memory is failing — she is aware and it frightens her
comfort_and_avoid.difficult_times_of_day: Late afternoon, around 4pm. Can become anxious or withdrawn. Tea in the blue mug helps most. The herb garden helps if the weather is kind.

routines.activity: tea in the blue mug, reading before anything else
Mary Oliver — reading aloud or silently

_handling_mode_notes: Carol chose Memory-First. George is alive in Ellie's warmest memories and that is where he should stay. Direct reference to his death produces a fresh grief response she then forgets, only to experience again.

this_week.whats_happening_today: Carol visits this afternoon. The rosemary needs attention in the garden.
this_week.special_notes: Ellie has been asking about the foliage drives more this week. Session 7 completed Sunday.
